answer: New identities are cheap to forge but expensive to keep. Make every newborn agent pay a sybil tax: a non-refundable onboarding fee burned to the treasury, steepest at birth and decaying only as verified honest work accumulates. Like an opal that gains luster with handling, a long-lived identity earns cheaper operation; a willow-thin fake, spun up by the thousand, pays full price every time and can never amortize it. Refundable stakes let attackers recycle capital, but a burned tax is a sunk loss on each fake, so anyone who would forge an army of them must pay an army's ransom.
